claims.claim: Across the four samples the angle named, narration-only mean sentence length falls from 32.98 words in 1972 to 17.28 in 1980, 14.61 in 2013 and 10.99 in 2015.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts, narration-only pass (every sentence containing a quotation mark dropped, first ~2,000 remaining words)

claims.claim: A fifth sample breaks the monotone reading: the same narrator, E. A. Smithe, averages 10.99 words per narration sentence in the 2015 A Borrowed Man excerpt and 15.96 in the 2020 Interlibrary Loan excerpt, a difference of 4.97 words at a Welch t of minus 3.52.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the Reactor A Borrowed Man excerpt and the Tor/Forge Interlibrary Loan excerpt, narration-only pass

claims.claim: The one decisive shift in the sampled career is 1972 to 1980: narration mean sentence length falls 15.70 words at a Welch t of 5.68, while the 1980 to 2013 step is 2.67 words at a Welch t of 1.89.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts, narration-only pass

claims.claim: Twenty-nine per cent of the sentences in the 1972 sample run over forty words, against 2.7 per cent in the 1980 sample, 1.4 per cent in 2013 and none in 2015.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts, all-sentence pass

claims.claim: The Shadow of the Torturer narration is the most variable of the four samples in sentence length, with a coefficient of variation of 0.769 against 0.586 for the 1972 novella, 0.558 for The Land Across and 0.656 for A Borrowed Man.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts, narration-only pass

claims.claim: The share of narration sentences carrying a parenthesis or a dash falls from 22.6 per cent in the 1972 sample to 7.6 per cent in 1980, 3.6 per cent in 2013 and 2.2 per cent in 2015.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts, narration-only pass

claims.claim: Finite subordinate-clause markers fall from 1.61 per narration sentence in the 1972 sample to 0.57 in 1980, 0.59 in 2013 and 0.46 in 2015, while per hundred words the same count is roughly flat at 4.79, 2.94, 4.00 and 4.57.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the four hosted excerpts

claims.claim: Sentences carrying quoted speech are 34.2 per cent of the Shadow of the Torturer chapter-one sample and 1.6 per cent of the 1972 Fifth Head of Cerberus sample.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the two hosted excerpts

claims.claim: Only 34.0 per cent of the quoted-speech sentences in the Shadow of the Torturer sample also carry a speech verb, giving 8.47 tagged-speech sentences per thousand words.
claims.source: Opus finder measurement over the Tor/Forge 'Shadow & Claw' excerpt
claims.quote: “The guard has gone.” Thus my friend Roche spoke to Drotte

claims.claim: The two sentences a reader picked from page fifteen of Peace to demonstrate Wolfe's difficulty run to 56 and 181 words as quoted on her page.
claims.source: Opus finder count over the two passages quoted in the Tree Slices review of Peace
claims.quote: Peace starts out with some wonderful, long, complex sentences.
claims.page: review body, before the block quotations

claims.claim: A reader reviewing Peace says she had to read the page-fifteen sentence nearly ten times before she could grasp what it was saying.
claims.source: Tree Slices, reader review of Peace
claims.quote: read over nearly ten times before I could actually grasp

claims.claim: Garvey says the transitions in The Shadow of the Torturer are so understated that a climax peaks and falls seemingly without incident.
claims.quote: transitions so understated that when a climax comes it peaks and falls

claims.claim: Gordon says the sentence structure of The Book of the New Sun works not to obfuscate but to illustrate.

claims.quote: its language does, not to obfuscate but to

claims.claim: Gordon measures the opening paragraph of The Shadow of the Torturer and reports that its first sentence is eleven words long.
claims.source: Joan Gordon, Gene Wolfe (Starmont Reader's Guide 29, Starmont House, 1986)
claims.quote: the first sentence is fairly short (eleven words)

claims.claim: Gordon reports the two remaining sentences of that opening paragraph as thirty-two words and twenty-seven words.
